title: Without a seen necessity linking neurons to qualia, qualia stay explanatorily idle

statements.text: No one can see why a pattern of neural activity should be accompanied by pain, or by any phenomenal quality. That is no proof that no such necessity holds, but without insight into it, a sufficient explanation of behavior uses only neural properties, and the connection to qualia explains nothing about how qualities make a difference. Because this gap has not closed for qualia, the traditional arguments about epiphenomenalism remain relevant.

sources.quote: Inability to see any such necessity is, of course, not a proof that such a necessity does not obtain.

Because this difficulty has not been removed in the case of qualia, the success or failure of the previously discussed Traditional Arguments remains relevant to contemporary thinking about epiphenomenalism.
